$comment: What the travel agent is allowed to draw. This prunes the PROMPT, not any renderer — every client keeps its full component registry, so nothing about a Web, Swift, Kotlin or Flutter client changes when a name leaves this list. Applied by `skillgen --prune`, which mirrors A2uiCatalog.with_pruning from the Python agent SDK.
why: What the agent may draw. Everything else is pruned out of the prompt before the model ever sees it — the renderers keep their full registries, so nothing about a client changes. The rule is that a basic component survives only when no travel component already does its job: layout and input primitives stay, and the generic display containers go, because the travel catalog exists precisely so the model says *what* it is showing rather than how to draw it.
whyFunctions: The rest of the catalog's functions are check-rule validators — required, regex, length, numeric, email — plus the boolean combinators that compose them. They exist for a `checks=` argument this agent never writes, and they cost more prompt than the six pruned components put together. The formatters stay: they are what makes a surface recompute on screen without a model turn.

excluded.AudioPlayer: no audio in a trip planner
excluded.Video: no video in a trip planner
excluded.Modal: the conversation is the modal; a surface that covers the chat hides the record
excluded.Tabs: the three surfaces are the navigation; tabs inside one of them compete with it
excluded.Divider: Column spacing already separates sections, and the model reaches for it as filler
excluded.Icon: ActivityItem takes a `category` and draws its own icon; WeatherStrip and the rest do the same. Nothing in the examples or in live traffic ever drew a bare one.
excluded.Image: HotelCard carries `imageUrl` and MapPreview draws itself. A loose image on a travel surface is a picture with no caption and no role.
excluded.Card: FlightOption, HotelCard, StatTile and PriceSummary *are* the cards, and they align across siblings in a way a generic container cannot. Keeping both taught the model two ways to draw a hotel.

whyComponents.DateTimeInput: One date, for a hop. It was excluded on the grounds that "DateRangePicker covers every date question this agent asks", and that stops being true the moment a route has more than one hop: four cities is four departure dates, and each one is a date, not a range. With nothing else to reach for the model invented `DateInput` and the surface did not compile — measured as the worst of the three opening scenarios.
